content: The omission of these questions was determined not to introduce bias into the guideline. The importance of screening and treating asymptomatic women with lower genital tract infections remains a key focus for this guideline. For pregnant women, what is the prognostic value of tests designed to detect lower genital tract infections compared to the reference standard in identifying risk factors for adverse outcomes? For pregnant women, does the administration of prophylactic antibiotics to prevent infectious events, as opposed to no intervention, reduce morbidity and improve clinical outcomes? The exclusion of these questions was not considered to compromise the integrity of the guideline. A dedicated WHO guideline on vaccinations during pregnancy needs to be developed. For pregnant women, does vaccination against viral influenza, compared to no vaccination, reduce morbidity and improve clinical outcomes? The omission of this question was not deemed to bias the guidelines. For pregnant women, does iodine supplementation, compared to no intervention, reduce morbidity and improve clinical outcomes? A new guideline addressing iodine supplementation is currently under development. World Health Organization, Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health, 20 Avenue Appia, 1211 Geneva 27, Switzerland.
